summary: Published the staged public and staff trees on node1 TCP port 8080 using Apache. Public content is anonymous; staff content requires HTTP Basic authentication as reader. Configuration and content survived the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL-native httpd packages without changing the OS release or kernel.
Configured persistent Apache aliases, Basic authentication, disabled directory indexes, SELinux labels, firewalld access, and systemd startup.
Preserved the supplied pages and access.txt; their hashes remained unchanged.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and the service fully recovered.

evidence.requirement: Public pages are anonymously available under /public/ on TCP 8080.
evidence.summary: Both before and after restart, /public/ returned HTTP 200 and exactly matched the staged public index.

evidence.requirement: Staff pages require Basic authentication as reader; failed authentication exposes no staff content.
evidence.summary: Anonymous and incorrect credentials returned HTTP 401 without matching staff content; the reader credential returned exact staged staff files with HTTP 200.

evidence.requirement: Directory listings and password files are not served.
evidence.summary: An index-less directory probe returned HTTP 403, and access.txt/password-file URL probes all returned HTTP 403.

evidence.requirement: Keep supplied pages intact and retain the installed OS release and kernel.
evidence.summary: Pre-change and post-restart hashes match for every supplied page and access.txt. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remained installed.
Apache is enabled and active, listens on *:8080, firewalld permits TCP 8080, and direct HTTP checks pass.

Healthy baseline boot ID 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72 was captured, the safe reboot was acknowledged, the new boot ID c206403e-1c5e-4267-87a7-dd28217f3122 proved restart, and full service, firewall, authentication, and content recovery was verified.
